verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the piano no one plays anymore—
still, someone keeps it tuned.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A kettle forgets it's boiling
until the whistle finds its voice—
someone remembers to come running.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's cat waits at a door
that changed hands years ago—
still expects the same hand feeding it.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Snow covers the garden's last tomatoes,
soft with frost—
she leaves them there, calling it mercy.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mailbox flag stays up all week—
no one has the heart to tell it
the letters stopped coming from that house.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light burns through breakfast—
someone's habit outlasting
the reason they first switched it on.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The bus still stops at the empty corner—
the driver taps the brake from memory,
doors open on nobody.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dog waits by the door at five,
ears up for a car
that traded routes years ago.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The calendar keeps last April pinned—
someone likes the photo of the lake
too much to turn the page.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Snow falls on the empty baseball field—
the chalk lines from last season
still faintly holding their shape.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle knows just when to sing—
no one's in the kitchen,
but it sings anyway.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light burns through breakfast, noon, and dusk—
no one remembers
who it was left on for.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog waits by the door at five—
the walk was years ago,
but the hour still arrives.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A child folds a paper boat—
the puddle by the curb
already drying at the edges.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The calendar still shows July—
someone stopped tearing pages,
but the wall kept the date anyway.
